biteOfDay: Bass on Table Rock have settled into classic fall patterns, holding on long points, gravel roll-offs, and offshore structure in 20-40+ feet as they feed aggressively ahead of winter. Mixed-bag action includes walleye on points and crappie around brush. On Taneycomo, rainbows remain aggressive with browns becoming more active and territorial in the upper stretches. Recent local reports (tablerockfi

tableRock.clarity: Gin-clear near dam; verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Insider tip: With light flows this morning, target Table Rock bass on secondary points and gravel banks in 15-30 feet using a football jig (brown/green with orange or chartreuse trailer) or a jighead minnow. On Taneycomo, drift or wade seams with 2-lb test and a Berkley Pink PowerWorm, 1/16-oz marab
